title: Zoom for consultants on Mac: client calls, recordings and voice help with Lazur in 2026
metaTitle: Zoom for consultants on Mac: setup, plan limits and tips for 2026
description: Set up Zoom for consultants on Mac: check plan limits, record with consent, share one window and get voice help mid-call from Lazur.
intro: Zoom for consultants on Mac works like Zoom for anyone else, with a few settings that matter more on client calls. Install the Zoom Workplace desktop app, check your plan's meeting limit, and set audio, recording and screen sharing before the first client joins. Lazur, a voice assistant for the Mac, can answer questions and walk you through steps while the call runs.
tldr: Zoom Workplace runs on macOS 10.15 or later. Zoom recommends 16 GB of RAM.
The free Basic plan ends meetings at 40 minutes and allows 100 participants. Check this before a long client call.
Pro lifts the meeting length to 30 hours and adds 10 GB of cloud recording per license.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur about anything on screen during the call.

blocks.text: Set up Zoom for consultants on Mac before the first client joins

Do this setup on a quiet day, not five minutes before a client joins. Open Zoom > Settings and test the audio and video with the headset and camera you will use on the call. The built-in microphone picks up keyboard noise, and a headset usually sounds clearer. Check that your Mac uses the headset as its input, not the laptop mic.

Zoom's desktop redesign moved some controls. In Zoom Workplace 6.7, meeting settings moved into one panel on the right side of the meeting window. If a setting seems missing, check that panel first, then the Zoom > Settings window.

items: Zoom > Settings > Audio: choose the microphone and speaker, then run the test.
Zoom > Settings > Video: pick the camera and preview it in the light you will use.
Zoom > Settings > Recording: choose where recordings are saved before you need one.
Zoom > About Zoom: confirm you are on the current release before a big call.

blocks.text: The most common setup mistake is testing audio inside a meeting that has already started. Use a personal meeting room instead. Ask a colleague to join and talk for a few sentences. Listen to their side of the call, because your own preview sounds different.
Mac requirements for Zoom Workplace in 2026

Zoom's desktop client needs macOS 10.15 (Catalina) or later. The minimum is 4 GB of RAM, and Zoom recommends 16 GB. The processor minimum is a dual-core 2 GHz chip. Zoom recommends a quad-core 2.5 GHz chip.

Starting with Zoom Workplace 7.0.0, macOS 10.13 and 10.14 are no longer supported. Zoom Workplace 6.7.7 is the last release for macOS below 10.15. If your Mac runs an older system, update macOS first. Otherwise you may be stuck on 6.7.7.

This page could not confirm the newest Mac build. Zoom's What's New page lists no desktop version numbers, and its only Mac item covers Zoom Rooms. The 7.0.0 client rolls out progressively starting March 23, 2026. Confirm your version in Zoom > About Zoom before you quote one to your IT team.
Zoom plan limits that change how you run client calls

Plan limits decide how long a call runs, how many people can join, and where recordings go. Start with the free Basic plan. Zoom's pricing page lists 40 minutes per meeting and 100 participants on Basic. Recording on Basic stays local to your Mac.
Pro lifts meeting length to 30 hours. It adds 10 GB of cloud recording per license, polling, and 8 custom meeting summary templates each month. Breakout rooms are listed on every plan.

Business raises the participant limit to 300, up from 100 on Pro. Zoom's small-business page lists a Large Meetings add-on for up to 1,000 attendees. That same page gives two different user ranges for one plan, so confirm the numbers with Zoom before you buy for a team.
A worked example with the 40-minute cap

Say you run a check-in with a client's leadership team and it runs long. On Basic, Zoom ends the meeting at 40 minutes. You then start a new meeting and send the link again, and people lose their place. On Pro, the same meeting fits under the 30-hour limit. The participant count stays under the 100 cap on both plans.

One gap is still open. Zoom's free video conferencing page does not say whether one-on-one calls have a time limit. Third-party guides disagree. Assume the 40-minute cap applies until you test it. Run a long one-on-one on a spare account the week before a big call.
Recording a Zoom call on Mac without losing the file

Zoom records in two places. Local recording saves to your Mac. Cloud recording saves to Zoom's servers. On Pro, each license gets 10 GB of cloud storage. A long video call can use a lot of that, so download cloud files and remove them once the client has a copy.

Choose the recording type before the meeting starts. Go to Zoom > Settings > Recording and set the save location. Menu labels may shift after the 7.0.0 redesign, so look for the Recording section if the path has moved.

items: Tell the client you are recording, and wait for a clear yes.
Check your engagement contract for rules on recording and file storage.
Save a local copy on your Mac, then delete the cloud version when the project closes.
Name the file with the client name, the topic and the date.

blocks.text: The usual mistake is forgetting that recording is on. Ask your client to say so out loud at the start. Then keep the recording indicator visible on your side of the call.
Screen sharing without showing client files by accident

Press ⌘ ⇧ S to start screen sharing in most Zoom meetings. Then choose one window, not the whole desktop. A desktop share shows every notification, every open tab, and every file name in your Dock. A single window keeps the rest of your Mac private.
Turn on a Focus before the call, from Control Center in the menu bar. Close mail and chat apps you do not need. Then share only the deck or spreadsheet the client will see.

macOS can block screen sharing until you allow Zoom. On recent macOS versions, look under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording. That path came from third-party guides, so check it on your macOS version the day before a call.
The classic error is sharing the whole screen to show one slide. Before you share, check which window is in front. Then check what the Dock and menu bar show.
Breakout rooms, polls and whiteboards for consultant workshops
Breakout rooms are listed on every plan, according to Zoom's pricing page. Use them for small group work, then bring everyone back for a readout. Plan the groups in advance so the rooms start fast.
Polls are listed on Pro and Business. Use one poll to rank options before a discussion. The room then sees the result before anyone argues for a favorite.

Whiteboards differ by plan. Zoom's small-business page lists 3 editable whiteboards on Basic and unlimited boards on Business. The same page says several people can share and annotate at the same time, which helps during a working session.
Breakout room limits are not settled. Sources quoted different room counts and different pre-assignment counts. Check Zoom's current help article before you promise a client a specific room number.
Meeting summaries, notes and client hours after the call

My Notes generates meeting summaries at no additional cost with an eligible paid plan. Zoom's small-business page says so. Pro also includes 8 custom meeting summary templates each month. The pricing page lists no template allowance for Business.

Templates help when the summary has to match a deliverable. Build one for decisions, one for risks and one for next steps. Use the same template for each client, so the summaries line up when you compare projects.
Track client hours appears on the same small-business page. It keeps records of billable hours and simplifies invoicing. Log the time right after the call, while the details are fresh.
Do not send an AI summary to a client unread. Check names, figures and commitments first. A summary can get a name or a number wrong, and the client will notice.
After the call, you can ask Lazur to draft a follow-up email from the notes you paste in. Lazur types the draft for you to review. It does not send anything on your behalf.
Keep client calls short enough to stay sharp

A 2024 study by Hadar Nesher Shoshan and Wilken Wehrt, published in the Journal of Occupational Health Psychology, looked at this question. It sampled 125 employees in Germany who worked at least 20 hours a week and attended video meetings regularly. Surveys ran four times a day over ten working days.

The study covered 590 workdays and 945 distinct meetings. It found video meetings were not related to higher exhaustion than non-video meetings. Video meetings under 44 minutes were less draining than other formats. That advantage disappeared for longer meetings.
Boring video meetings were linked to slightly higher exhaustion. So the agenda matters more than the screen. A short call with a clear purpose usually beats a long one with no plan.

This page relies on PsyPost's summary, because the journal article was not opened. The participants were employees, not consultants. Treat the 44-minute figure as a planning guide. A 40-minute kickoff with one decision and one owner list fits well. A longer working session needs a planned break or a second call.
Ask Lazur for help during a Zoom call on Mac
Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud, so you can keep your eyes on the client and the call.

Lazur points at things. Ask where something is, and it draws a circle and a label around it on your screen. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it gives the next step. Lazur does not click buttons or operate Zoom for you.
Hold fn to dictate. Lazur types clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots help with client names, product terms and standard replies.

items: Where is the record button? Lazur points. You click.
How do I share only one window? Lazur guides you one step at a time.
What does this error mean? Lazur explains what is on screen.
Open the shared agenda in my browser. Lazur opens the link.

blocks.text: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Your client agreement still decides what you may show, so check it before you ask about confidential material.
Mistakes consultants make in Zoom on Mac

items: Joining on a Mac with a low battery and no charger. Plug in before you start.
Sharing the whole desktop when one window would do.
Recording without saying so, or leaving cloud files that never got downloaded.
Running a long workshop on the free plan, then losing the room when the meeting ends at 40 minutes.
Updating Zoom on the morning of a big call. Update a day early, then test audio and screen sharing.

blocks.text: Most of these take a few minutes to prevent. Set the checks once, then reuse them for each client. The checks cost less time than a restart in front of a client.
Edge cases to check before a big client call
Check permissions after macOS updates. Screen sharing and recording permissions can need a second look after a system update. Open System Settings and recheck them the day before the call.

Check the Mac you will present from. A work laptop with a managed Zoom install may behave differently from a home Mac. Confirm which Zoom build your company uses, because IT policy can hold back updates.
Lazur runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Zoom's own requirements still apply to the Zoom app, so check those too.
What to do next with Zoom and Lazur

Start on the free plan if your calls stay under 40 minutes and do not need cloud recordings. Move to Pro when sessions run longer or you need more recording space. Compare plans on Zoom's pricing page, and confirm the details there before you pay.

If you want voice help during calls, [download Lazur](/download) and try it on your next internal call. Lazur's plans and trial are on the [pricing page](/pricing). For more on the Zoom side, read [Lazur for Zoom on Mac](/apps/zoom).

If your work is mostly spreadsheets and decks, see [Excel for consultants on Mac](/for/consultants/excel) and [PowerPoint for consultants on Mac](/for/consultants/powerpoint). Both pages cover the files you share during the same calls.

faq.question: Does Zoom for consultants on Mac need a paid plan?
faq.answer: Not always. The free Basic plan works for calls that stay under 40 minutes with up to 100 participants, according to Zoom's pricing page. Move to Pro when calls run longer or when you need cloud recording with more space.

faq.question: Which macOS version does Zoom need in 2026?
faq.answer: Zoom Workplace needs macOS 10.15 or later. Zoom 7.0.0 dropped support for macOS 10.13 and 10.14, and Zoom Workplace 6.7.7 is the last release for macOS below 10.15. Zoom recommends 16 GB of RAM.

faq.question: Can I record a Zoom call on my Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Basic recording stays local to your Mac. Go to Zoom > Settings > Recording to set the save location. Tell the client first and wait for a clear yes. Pro adds 10 GB of cloud recording per license.

faq.question: Does Lazur join my Zoom call or record it?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Zoom, and it does not operate Zoom for you. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut, so it is not sitting in the call.

faq.question: Is it safe to ask Lazur about a client screen?
faq.answer: Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Your client agreement still decides what you may show, so check it first.

faq.question: Can Lazur click Zoom buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It draws a circle and a label around a control, or guides you one click at a time while it waits for each click.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Intel Macs?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Zoom's own requirements still apply to the Zoom app, so check those separately before a big client call.
